I have farmed these same 5 mu in Quzhou for 50 years, and my father farmed them before me. Wheat-maize double cropping is the only system I know — it keeps the land working and gives my family two chances a year. My wife and I handle most of the day-to-day work because our sons have off-farm jobs in the county town; they can only come back for harvest and planting peaks. At 70, I do not chase new tricks. I do what has not failed me.

For wheat, I will sow my usual improved variety in mid-October after turning the maize stubble with the rotary tiller. The extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I have always done a bit more to be safe — I will put down about 15 kg N per mu, plus 6 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium through compound fertilizer. I split it: base dressing at planting, then urea topdressing when the wheat greens up and again at jointing. I irrigate three times — wintering water, jointing, and grain filling — because the well water costs money, but wheat cannot dry out at those stages. Two pesticide sprays are enough if you watch the fields: one for weeds, one for aphids or rust if they show up. I expect around 480 kg per mu if spring does not turn too dry.

For maize, there is no time to waste after wheat harvest in early June. I plant hybrid seed the same day or the next using the no-till seeder — everyone here does that now, or you miss the heat. I give it about 17 kg N, 6 kg P, and 5 kg K per mu, side-dressed at the big flare stage. Summer rain usually helps, but I will irrigate twice if it turns dry, especially at flowering. Two sprays: one herbicide, one for corn borer. Hybrid seed should give me about 520 kg per mu in a normal year. I keep inputs moderate because my pockets are not deep, and at my age a total crop failure would be hard to recover from.
